name: Dr. Samir RACHIDI
roles: Director General of the Institute for Research in Solar Energy and New Energies (IRESEN)
Secretary General of the Moroccan Green Hydrogen Cluster (Cluster Green H2)
paragraphs: Samir Rachidi is Director General of the Institute for Research in Solar Energy and New Energies (IRESEN). Together with his team, he develops research projects and demonstration activities focused on Power-to-X, green chemistry, energy storage, concentrated solar power (CSP), and the hybridisation of solar energy and bioenergy.

Before taking up his current position, Samir was responsible for the R&D programme at the Moroccan Agency for Sustainable Energy (MASEN). His role involved catalysing national R&D efforts in solar energy, establishing partnerships and collaborations for international R&D projects in solar applications, and contributing to a strategic R&D direction to help unlock Morocco's future industrial potential in the solar sector.

Previously, he worked as an R&D engineer at a start-up called RespInnovation in Sophia Antipolis, France. In 2011, Samir earned a doctorate in hydrogen proton-exchange membrane (PEM) fuel cells, carried out jointly at CEA Grenoble and the CNRS Pprime Institute in Poitiers, both in France.

Samir holds a dual Master of Science and Engineering degree in chemical, environmental and energy engineering, awarded by the École des Mines de Saint-Étienne and Jean Monnet University in 2008. He also lectures at Mohammed VI Polytechnic University (UM6P) and École Centrale Casablanca.

He was recently elected Secretary General of the Moroccan Green Hydrogen Cluster (Cluster Green H2). He also leads the green hydrogen task force of the Green Economy Commission within the General Confederation of Moroccan Enterprises (CGEM).
